items.title: Cyclone-hit villages in Prakasam district remain without electricity
points: Since Cyclone Murasu hit the coastline of Andhra Pradesh, several villages in Nagulappalapadu, Kanigiri, Kothapatnam, Singarayakonda, and Addanki mandals of Prakasam district have been facing continuous power outages.

Though the Andhra Pradesh Central Power Distribution Company Limited (APCPDCL) staff are undertaking restoration works on war-footing basis, the residents in these coastal villages are spending their nights by using oil lamps and candles.
According to source, the villagers are going to the nearest urban centre to charge their mobile phones at a cost of ₹10 per charge.
For more than a week, the Electricity department personnel have been restoring the electric poles and overhead wires that were damaged by the cyclone.

However, the power supply has not yet been restored, leaving many villages in darkness Speaking to The Hindu, Energy Minister Gottipati Ravi Kumar said, “Initially, we have estimated an overall expenditure of ₹500 crore to repair the electric…

items.title: Delhi SIR: Form 6 applications cross 3L-mark after draft roll excludes 47.5 lakh voters
points: More than 3 lakh applications seeking fresh enrolment in Delhi's electoral roll have been filed since the publication of the draft roll on August 31, which excluded around 47.5 lakh voters, according to official data.
A total of 3,00,431 Form 6 applications, used by voters to seek inclusion in the electoral roll, were received between August 31 and November 9, data showed.

The Delhi election authorities will start generating fresh enumeration forms for all 47.5 lakh electors excluded from the draft roll as part of a re-verification exercise to facilitate their inclusion in the final electoral roll, to be published on…

The exercise will cover electors marked as absent, shifted, dead and duplicate (ASDD) during the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) exercise, including those who shifted from one place to another within Delhi but were left out of the draft roll.
The data also showed that 30,490 Form 7 applications, which seek deletion of names from the electoral roll, were received between August 31 and November 9.

items.title: Sugarcane farmers urge industries for at least ₹5,000 per tonne
points: Citing the prices in neighbouring States including Maharashtra, the farmers have asked them to consider expenditure on fertilizers, labour, diesel and others to come to a conclusion.
Various aspects pertaining to sugarcane cultivation and procurement were discussed at a meeting on the prices held by Sangareddy Additional Collector T.L.
Sangeetha with representatives of factories, farmers organisations and others, at the Collectorate on Tuesday (November 10, 2026).
The Additional Collector suggested the representatives to consider the welfare of farmers and development of industries in taking the decision in two to three days.

items.title: NDA wrests Kadapa ZPTCs from YSRCP
points: Jagan Mohan Reddy, the TDP-led NDA swept most of the ZPTC and MPTC constituencies in the recent elections.
Of the sixteen ZPTC seats that went to polls, the TDP bagged 12 and its ally Jana Sena won two, leaving the other two to YSRCP.
TDP zonal coordinator Reddeppagari Srinivasa Reddy, Pulivendula TDP in-charge B.Tech Ravi, and government whip C.
Adinarayana Reddy (Jammalamadugu BJP MLA) left no stone unturned to ensure the victory of NDA in Kadapa, which was once considered the YSRCP’s stronghold.
Pulivendula, the home constituency of Mr. Jagan Mohan Reddy, gave a unique result this time, as it came both as a let-down as well as a face-saver for the YSRCP.
Both the Vempalle and Vemula ZPTC seats won by the YSRCP in Kadapa district are from this constituency.
Veteran politician and TDP former State vice-president Putha Narasimha Reddy is a major aspirant for the Kadapa ZP chairperson’s post.

items.title: Vinod Kumar urges govt. to run direct RTC buses to AIIMS Bibinagar from all Dist. HQs
points: Former Member of Parliament and Bharat Rashtra Samithi (BRS) leader B.

Vinod Kumar has requested the State Government to instruct the Telangana State Road Transport Corporation (TGSRTC) to provide bus connectivity to AIIMS Bibinagar in Yadadri Bhuvanagiri district, ensuring convenient access to quality healthcare for people…
In a letter to Minister for Transport Ponnam Prabhakar and Vice-Chairman and Managing Director of TGSRTC Y.
Nagi Reddy, Mr. Vinod Kumar requested for introduction of direct bus services connecting AIIMS Bibinagar with all District Headquarters in the State.

Further, he sought frequent and dedicated bus services between Uppal Junction, Hyderabad, and AIIMS Bibinagar, preferably at intervals of 30 minutes during peak hospital hours, subject to passenger demand and operational feasibility.
Recalling the efforts behind the establishment of AIIMS in Telangana, he stated that the then Chief Minister K.
Chandrashekhar Rao had taken the initiative in 2016 by representing the matter to the Prime Minister, while TRS (now BRS) MPs pursued the demand with the Union Government.

items.title: Nifty PSU Bank Index Performance: Bank of India, UCO Bank among 7 stocks rebound 15–56% from 1-yr lows - here’s why
points: Shares of state-owned banks such as SBI, Bank of Maharashtra, and Indian Bank have been flying high lately as Dalal Street staged a strong rebound.
In the previous session, the Nifty PSU Bank index surged nearly 4%, marking its biggest single-day gain in almost two years.

Union Bank of India, Punjab National Bank, Bank of India, and Bank of Baroda emerged as the top gainers, with all 12 constituents of the index closing higher, posting gains ranging between 0.7% and 5.6%.
To be precise, PSU bank stocks have been in recovery mode since late October, gaining around 12% from their recent lows.
FPIs have pumped ₹53,739 crore into domestic stocks in November so far, according to NSDL data.
The recent rally has helped most PSU bank stocks recover sharply from their respective 52-week lows, with Bank of Maharashtra leading the pack with a 58% rebound.

items.title: Nine cases booked during checks at rice shops in Peddapalli district, special rice sale counters opened in Peddapalli, Khammam towns
points: As many as nine cases were booked for short-weighing of rice bags and other violations during surprise inspections at around 50 wholesale and retail rice shops across Peddapalli district recently.
According to official sources, the inspections were conducted to curb the sale of rice at prices above the MRP, short-weighing of rice bags and other violations.
The special drive assumes significance in the wake of complaints about soaring rice prices and alleged irregularities by some traders in various parts of the district.
Officials have instructed rice traders to prominently display boards at their outlets detailing the prices of different varieties of rice and their respective stock positions, sources added.

Meanwhile, a special sale counter was opened at Kanakadurga Traders in Peddapalli town on Tuesday under the aegis of the Civil Supplies Department to make quality rice available to consumers at government-prescribed prices for different varieties.
In Khammam, the department opened its second special sale counter at the Integrated Market in VDO’s Colony on Tuesday, according to a press release.

items.title: Pranab Mukherjee hinted at desire to become PM, ‘shocked’ me, writes Sonia Gandhi
points: Former President Pranab Mukherjee had “shocked” Sonia Gandhi by hinting at his “long-held desire” to become Prime Minister during a conversation with her in 2010, suggesting that perhaps it was time for a “change at the top”, the former Congress president…
The book, published by HarperCollins, was made available in bookstores on Tuesday (November 10, 2026), but the official launch is likely to take place on November 16.
Mukherjee, then a senior member of the Manmohan Singh Cabinet, had developed serious differences with the then Finance Minister P.
He would sometimes stay back for conversations with Ms. Gandhi after meetings of the Congress Strategy Group, which was set up to discuss parliamentary business.

“On one occasion, in 2010, I think after expressing his frustration, he shocked me with the suggestion that perhaps it was time for a change at the top, which I understood as a hint of his long-held desire to become Prime Minister,” she wrote.

items.title: Housing assistance instalments for 32,000 families this fiscal: Minister
points: The government is taking urgent steps to disburse the first and second instalments of housing assistance to 32,000 families this financial year through the departments of Scheduled Castes, Scheduled Tribes and Backward Classes, Minister for SC, ST and…
She was speaking after inaugurating the ‘Snehasparsham’ programme, organised by Kattakambal grama panchayat as part of its 2026-27 annual plan on Monday.
The programme included the distribution of financial assistance to dialysis patients, collection of used syringes from households and a medical camp.
The Life Mission housing assistance has been enhanced from ₹4 lakh to ₹6 lakh, while the allocation for housing for ST families has been raised to ₹8 lakh, the Minister said.
ST women are also eligible for assistance of up to ₹15 lakh for self-employment ventures, with a 75% subsidy.
Emergency medical assistance is available through the SC/ST departments in addition to the Chief Minister’s Distress Relief Fund.
SC families who lose their earning member are also eligible for emergency assistance of ₹2 lakh.

items.title: ‘Integrity is paramount, don’t forget your roots’: Revanth tells new DSPs
points: Revanth Reddy at the valedictory of training programme for Probationary Deputy Superintendents of Police in Hyderabad on Tuesday.
Revanth Reddy told the newly recruited DSPs not to forget their social and economic backgrounds or the circumstances that had brought them to the positions they occupied.
“Your knowledge, integrity and dedication have brought you here.
His comments come in the wake of several police officers being trapped by the Anti-Corruption Bureau (ACB) like never before.

“Police were often the first institution people approached when confronted with a problem, sometimes even before turning to their own families, he said asking the DSPs to preserve the credibility built by generations of upright police officers.
The State government had established the EAGLE Force to deal firmly with drug trafficking and consumption, he said.

Stating that the government had also introduced new institutional mechanisms to address drug control, food safety, traffic management and cybercrime, he said it was prepared to send newly recruited DSPs abroad for exposure and study of policing practices,…

items.title: India objects to Chinese influencers showing Bangladesh as Delhi, calls it ‘peddling false narratives’
points: India reacted strongly on Tuesday to reports of Chinese influencers filming videos in Bangladesh and passing them off as depictions of India, calling on authorities in Beijing and Dhaka to take action against those involved in presenting a “distorted…

Reports in the Bangladesh media said scores of Chinese vloggers and influencers were involved in a campaign of shooting videos in the impoverished neighbourhoods of Uttara and Tekpara in Dhaka and passing off their broadcasts as originating in New Delhi.

Prothom Alo, a leading Bangladeshi daily, said in a lengthy investigative report that more than 150 Chinese nationals have been involved in filming videos and livestreaming in Uttara and Tekpara, both densely populated and property-stricken areas,…
During a livestream from Uttara on November 1, a Chinese woman said: “This is New Delhi.
Rezaul Hasan Laskar is Foreign Editor with the Hindustan Times, which he joined in 2015.

items.title: Madras High Court restrains thermal power plant workers from going on strike
points: The Madras High Court on Tuesday (November 10, 2026) restrained Central Organisation of Tamil Nadu Electricity Employees, affiliated to the Centre of Indian Trade Unions (CITU), from going on a strike at the State government run thermal power plants from…

Rajesh Vivekananthan issued the interim injunction pursuant to an urgent public interest litigation petition filed by activist Vineeth Kumar who feared that public utilities would suffer if power generation gets disrupted due to the strike.
The judges also recorded the submission of Additional Advocate General P.V.

Balasubramaniam that there was no direct employer-employee relationship between the Tamil Nadu Power Generation Corporation Limited (TNPGCL) and the workers who had been engaged for work through various contractors.
Yet, the workers had raised a host of demands and threated to strike work if their demands were not met.

The Additional Advocate General said that the thermal power generation plants must keep functioning round-the-clock and that it would become very difficult to restart them if there happened to be a temporary shutdown.

items.title: Banks in Telangana achieved 74% of Kharif loan targets in H1
points: Total deposits of banks in Telangana increased by ₹23,356 crore during the quarter that ended in September to ₹10,16,303 crore, while total advances rose ₹46,050 crore to ₹13,22,798 crore.
The Credit-Deposit (CD) ratio continues to be above 100% despite global and domestic challenges.
It stood at 130.16% at the end of the quarter, said Neelesh Dwivedi, CGM of SBI Hyderabad Circle.

Presenting the performance of the banks at the review meeting of the State Level Bankers’ Committee (SLBC), for the quarter ending September, here on Tuesday, he said that during the first half year of the current financial year, banks disbursed ₹42,885…
The disbursements as investment credit to Agriculture Allied, Agriculture Infra and Agriculture Ancillary activities stood at ₹54,057 crore, which was 64.27% of the annual targets.
Banks disbursed ₹347 crore educational loans and ₹2,869 crore housing loans under Priority Sector during the first six months.

items.title: APCRDA, IOCL sign MoU to develop green energy infrastructure in Amaravati
points: An MoU to this effect was signed at the APCRDA headquarters in Rayapudi on Tuesday.
Vijay Rama Raju and IOCL Executive Director and State Head (Telangana and Andhra Pradesh State office) Piyush Mittal exchanged the agreement documents.

The partnership envisages exploring and developing city gas distribution networks, including piped natural gas (PNG) and compressed natural gas (CNG), battery-swapping stations, compressed biogas, green hydrogen and other low-carbon energy solutions.

As part of the initiative, the two organisations will prepare an Integrated Energy Master Plan to assess Amaravati's present and future energy requirements and develop sustainable transport and mobility infrastructure.
The agreement also envisages establishing modern multi-fuel energy stations and utility corridors equipped with smart energy management systems to improve commuter convenience.
A Joint Working Group comprising representatives of both organisations will oversee implementation, conduct technical studies and prepare Detailed Project Reports (DPRs).
Senior IOCL officials and APCRDA Economic Development Department representatives attended the programme.

items.title: GTA 6 Officially Targets 30 FPS on PS5 and Xbox, Confirms Rockstar
points: After weeks of speculation about whether GTA 6 would be locked at 30 FPS or offer higher frame rates on consoles like the PS5 Pro, Rockstar has officially confirmed a 30 FPS target across all PS5 and Xbox consoles, including the PS5 Pro.
This means a GTA 6 60 FPS mode isn’t possible at launch, though it could arrive later with next-generation consoles.
Rockstar also confirmed PS5 Pro-exclusive features, including improved clarity through PlayStation Spectral Super Resolution (PSSR) and ray-traced shadows.

Speaking of PS5-exclusive features, Rockstar has outlined several benefits coming to GTA 6 for PlayStation players at launch, including adjustable DualSense haptic feedback settings, Tempest 3D Audio support for more immersive sound, and faster loading times.
In the same Newswire blog, Rockstar also confirmed that GTA 6 will be playable on Xbox One thanks to Xbox Cloud Gaming, with support for Remote Play across both PlayStation and Xbox.
Like Red Dead Redemption 2, GTA 6 will run at 30 FPS at launch.

Highlighting the Centre’s focus on mineral security, the minister said 4,373 mineral exploration projects had been completed since 2014, including 1,724 related to critical minerals and 656 linked to rare earth elements.

Addressing a gathering after inaugurating three new facilities at the GSI campus in Hyderabad, including the International Hostel Complex, an Advanced Geophysical Data Processing Laboratory and the ‘Karmayogi’ Digital Studios, he said that the organisation…

Mr. Kishan Reddy noted that India’s mining sector was rapidly expanding and achieving global standards but the GSI must also enhance its international presence and capabilities through active collaboration with geological and exploration agencies across…
The minister underscored the importance of emerging technologies such as Artificial Intelligence, Machine Learning, remote sensing and advanced data analytics in mineral exploration.

Mr. Lalit Babu emerged victorious in two events, both held in Europe.
The Vijayawada-born player clinched the title at the 43rd Münsterland Chess Open in Germany, held between October 17 and 24.

items.title: Congress’s Ajay Maken questions omission of air pollution hearing from Home Affairs panel agenda
points: Congress leader and panel member Ajay Maken.

An agenda circulated on November 5 included a discussion on ‘Air pollution in Delhi-NCR: Enforcement of regulatory measures, effective implementation of GRAP measures, protection of vulnerable sections and coordination among law enforcement and government…
“I wish to register my objection to the omission of the air pollution hearing from the revised agenda for 17 November 2026.
He had first sought an examination of air pollution in a November 2 letter to the committee chairperson, Mr. Maken said.
“The original public notice dated 5 November scheduled the hearing with the Ministry of Home Affairs and concerned agencies for 17 November at 2 p.m.

Noting that no alternative date had been announced, Mr. Maken sought either restoration of the November 17 hearing or communication of the earliest possible date for discussion along with an explanation for the change.

Describing Delhi’s air pollution as a “public health emergency”, Mr. Maken said the protection of vulnerable groups, enforcement of regulations and coordination among agencies required immediate attention.

items.title: 22nd State Excise Arts and Sports meet begins in Kollam
points: The 22nd State Excise Arts and Sports Meet will take place from November 11 to 13 across three major venues in Kollam—Lal Bahadur Shastri Stadium, S.N.
District and zonal winners from across Kerala will compete in this State-level championship.
The athletic and sports events feature a wide range of games including football, volleyball, cricket, kabaddi, badminton, chess, and track and field events.
Meanwhile, all cultural competitions will be hosted across five stages at the Sree Narayana Guru Cultural Complex.
A ceremonial torch relay, arriving from Oachira with prominent athletes, will reach the Chinnakada Excise Complex to mark the prelude.
The official inauguration will be held on November 12 by Excise and Co-operation Minister M.
A colorful march-past featuring athletes from all 14 districts will kick off the ceremony, followed by the lighting of the flame and flag hoisting.
The meet will conclude with a valedictory session inaugurated by Women and Child Development Minister Bindhu Krishna.

items.title: KTU Syndicate accords priority to Vilappilsala campus development
points: Updated - November 10, 2026 08:59 pm IST - THIRUVANANTHAPURAM A Syndicate meeting of APJ Abdul Kalam Technological University (KTU) on Tuesday resolved to accord priority to the development of its permanent campus at Vilappilsala.
The meeting also approved the university’s annual plan proposal for 2027-28.
The proposal submitted to the State Planning Board included an allocation of ₹6.90 crore for the construction of a hostel on the campus.
KTU has also requested the government to sanction an additional amount of ₹30.90 crore for the campus development works approved for 2026-27.
The 2027-28 annual plan proposal also earmarks ₹3.94 crore for the university library, including books, journals and digital learning resources.

Besides, the plan includes provisions for the Digital Development Centre, KTU Future Labs, Urban Innovation Hub, a Centre of Excellence in Embedded Systems Technology, and new undergraduate and integrated postgraduate programmes in the university schools.
The Syndicate ratified disciplinary actions taken with the approval of the Vice-Chancellor in over 500 examination malpractice cases.

items.title: CPI(M) accuses UDF of making higher education sole privilege of students from entitled families and undermining reservation criteria

John of seeking to undermine government and aided higher education institutions, which offer affordable tutoring to students hailing from marginalised and economically underprivileged sections of society.

items.title: Oxford University transfers custodianship of 39 Naga ancestral remains to Naga people
points: The Oxford University Council in the UK officially transferred the custodianship of 39 Naga ancestral remains formerly held at the Pitt Rivers Museum (PRM) to the Naga people through the Forum for Naga Reconciliation (FNR) and the Naga tribal bodies.

“The Naga remains which had been under the custodianship of the Pitt Rivers Museum for over a century have now been formally returned to the care of the Naga communities in a solemn handover ceremony hosted by the Pitt Rivers Museum, University of Oxford…
Since the Pitt Rivers Museum was established in 1884, collectors have donated Naga artifacts including Naga ancestral human remains to the museum, an update from the FNR said on Monday.
The Naga repatriation ceremony where the remains were handed over was the culmination of a process that began in 2020 with the FNR as the facilitator.
The document was also attested by Visier Sanyü on behalf of the FNR, and Thejao Vihienuo as a representative of the Naga tribes.

During the operation, 10 people found loitering on the streets during late-night hours without any apparent reason were taken into custody, while 30 others were counselled and warned against involvement in criminal activities, the police said.
The police cautioned those counselled that strict action would be initiated if they were found engaging in unlawful activities.

items.title: Hospitals, medical shops not implementing reduced cancer drug prices to face action
points: Minister for Health, Medical and Family Welfare Satya Kumar Yadav Minister for Health, Medical and Family Welfare Satya Kumar Yadav has directed officials and drug inspectors across the State to conduct inspections to ensure that the revised cancer drug…

In October, the National Pharmaceutical Pricing Authority (NPPA) capped trade margins at 30% for 137 non-scheduled anti-cancer drugs, reducing the price of nearly 900 cancer medicine brands by up to 70%-93%.
The revised rates came into force from November 9.
In this connection, the Minister held a review meeting on Tuesday, November 10, with Health Secretary G.
Veerapandian, Director General of the Drugs Control Administration Arun Babu and other officials to discuss the measures to be implemented.
The Minister instructed officials to monitor the availability of medicines, implementation of revised prices and intensify inspections at hospitals and medical stores.
Charging more than the applicable price will not be permitted, the Minister said, detailing steps of action that need to be taken by drug inspectors against erring individuals.

items.title: Sabarimala gold theft case: requests for prosecution sanction made before authorities, SIT informs Kerala HC
points: The Special Investigation Team probing the Sabarimala gold theft case has informed the Kerala High Court that the request for sanction to prosecute the accused have been made before the Travancore Devaswom Board.
The prosecution sanction was requested in the case pertaining to the alleged removal of gold cladding from Sreekovil (sanctum sanctorum) of Sabarimala Ayyappa Temple.
Requests for sanction to prosecute four of the 13 accused were made to the Revenue (Devaswom) Department Secretary.

items.title: Binance Spots iOS Bug That Could Put Cryptocurrency Wallet Keys at Risk
points: November 10 security alert revealed that iOS 26.7.1, 27.0.1, and 27.2 were among the vulnerable software.
This vulnerability is associated with the application sandbox that is used by Apple to protect the company's products from access to the files of other apps.

This vulnerability was discovered in the worse_query research repository, where it was noted that the flaw enables an application to access directories that can be accessed only by other applications.
The proof of concept applies to iOS 26 and iOS 27 versions.
Nevertheless, Binance stated that if such files containing personal information were available to other applications due to the security flaw, then malicious apps would be able to access them.
As per the warning from Binance, the threat affects “the whole ecosystem,” including cryptocurrency wallets as well as other applications that hold sensitive information of customers.

items.title: OpenAI Introduces Control Room to Stop AI Models Quickly When Safety Concerns Arise
points: Control Room works by integrating the workload, the inference engine, and the centralised Control Room service.

Control Room can stop AI model output within 35 seconds of receiving an intervention request OpenAI has announced a new central system called Control Room to improve safety across its AI research infrastructure..
The new system is designed to track model workloads across the infrastructure and stop them when safety or security concerns arise.
The new system is advertised to halt model output within 35 seconds of an intervention decision.
In a blog post on Tuesday, OpenAI detailed the Control Room.
The company claims that the system can stop AI model output within 35 seconds of receiving an intervention request.
Whenever the job requests output from an AI model, the inference engine requests permission from Control Room to fulfil that request, passing the job_id along to Control Room.

items.title: Gurugram traffic police impounds motorcycle with pending challans worth ₹4.06 Lakh
points: The Gurugram traffic police on Tuesday impounded a motorcycle with 67 pending traffic challans involving outstanding fines of over ₹4 lakh, officials said.
The two-wheeler was seized during a checking drive at Damdama red light, they said.
During the inspection, a team led by zonal officer ASI Jaiveer stopped the motorcycle for verification and found 67 pending challans amounting to ₹4,06,500, a senior traffic police officer said.
Most of the challans were related to violations such as riding without a helmet, not having valid vehicle insurance and driving without a valid Pollution Under Control (PUC) certificate, he said.
The vehicle was impounded after its owner failed to produce the requisite documents, the officer added.
The traffic police has appealed to commuters to wear helmets while riding two-wheelers and ensure that all mandatory vehicle documents, including valid insurance and PUC certificates, are up to date.

items.title: Chinese Electric Hypercar Hits 503.17 Km/h, Sets Two Guinness Records
points: BYD's Yangwang U9 Xtreme has become the first production car to cross 500km/h in a verified single-direction speed run.
The electric hypercar reached 503.17km/h on a closed highway in Abu Dhabi on November 1, 2026, earning two Guinness World Records.
The attempt took place on Sheikh Khalifa Bin Zayed International Road, also known as the E11, in Abu Dhabi's Al Dhafra region.
The U9 Xtreme had already achieved 496.22km/h at the ATP Papenburg test facility in Germany in September 2025, also driven by Basseng.
The Abu Dhabi run improved that figure by 6.95km/h and crossed the 500km/h barrier that the earlier attempt had narrowly missed.
The standard Yangwang U9 recorded 309km/h during testing in China in January 2024 and 391.94km/h in Germany later that year.
The uprated Xtreme reached 472.41km/h in August 2025, before raising the figure to 496.22km/h the following month.

items.title: South Korea Looks to Position Jinhae New Port as Arctic Shipping Hub
points: (Source: Changwon city hall) The South Korean city of Changwon is seeking to position the planned Jinhae New Port as a future hub for Arctic shipping, linking the major port development project with the region’s established shipbuilding, machinery, and…
Jinhae New Port is a national infrastructure project designed to accommodate some of the world’s largest container ships.
Changwon’s latest proposal is not to build a separate Arctic port, but to incorporate the potential shipping route into the development of Jinhae New Port and its surrounding industrial base.
Changwon Mayor Kang Ki-yoon said the city wanted Jinhae, historically an important naval port, to take on a new role in the Arctic shipping era.
South Korea’s Arctic ambitions have gained momentum following the PanStar Acro’s round-trip voyage between Busan and Europe via the Northern Sea Route.
The 2,758-TEU container ship returned to Busan on October 11 after a 50-day voyage, demonstrating that a South Korean container vessel could complete the journey.

items.title: School Holiday: Check Which States Have Suspended Classes For Post-Diwali Festivities And Chhath Puja
points: School Holiday Update: The festival of Diwali was celebrated with great enthusiasm across the country on Sunday, November 8.
Consequently, schools in many states remained closed the next day on November 9.
Following Diwali, several major festivals, such as Bhai Dooj, Govardhan Puja, and Chhath Puja, are being observed.
According to the holiday calendar released by the state's Education Department for 2026, schools are scheduled to remain closed till November 17 for festivals including Bhai Dooj and Chhath Puja.
Schools will also observe a holiday on November 24 on the occasion of Guru Nanak Jayanti and Kartik Purnima.
According to the Jharkhand Academic Council's official calendar, November 11 has been marked as Bhaiya Dooj or Chitragupta Puja.
Additionally, the official calendar has announced November 15 and 16 as a restricted or optional holiday for Chhath Puja celebrations.
Several reports also suggest that some schools have holidays until November 15 in Maharashtra.

items.title: Satellite Images Capture Thick Smog Over Northern India 2 Days After Diwali
points: The toxic haze that has taken over much of northern India amid dropping temperatures, an annual event now, is so intense that it is visible from space.

A satellite view from the National Aeronautics and Space Administration (NASA) Worldview, an interactive web-based mapping and visualization tool, shows much of India covered in a thick, grey blanket on November 10.
The fog, as seen in the satellite view, also extends further north into the Himalayan states of Uttarakhand, Himachal Pradesh, and Jammu and Kashmir.
However, the satellite view of India today stands in contrast to yesterday, November 9, just a day after Diwali.

On November 9, the haze was seemingly thinner, scattered, and covering only a few parts of the country including Delhi, Uttar Pradesh, Bihar, and other northern states such as Uttarakhand, Himachal Pradesh, and Jammu and Kashmir.

BJP state secretary Vinoj P Selvam took aim at Vijay, asking, "Where is CM Vijay when the people of Tamil Nadu demand answers?" In a post on X, Selvam questioned how cybercriminals managed to access multiple government accounts and transfer crores of…
How were transactions worth crores executed?

Money entrusted to the government for the benefit of ordinary citizens," Selvam said, adding that Tamil Nadu needed transparent answers, stronger institutions and a government capable of protecting public money.
An online fraud involving the siphoning of ₹22.10 crore from Tamil Nadu government bank accounts came to light, police said on Tuesday.
Priyanjali Narayan is a journalist with Hindustan Times based in New Delhi.

items.title: Meghalaya Urges Centre To Compensate Landowners Along Bangladesh Border
points: With the Centre pushing to complete fencing along the India-Bangladesh international border, Meghalaya has sought a solution to a growing concern among landowners who could lose access to their agricultural plots once the barrier is built.
Meghalaya shares a 443-kilometre international border with Bangladesh.

The state government has approached the Centre, proposing that the government take over land falling beyond the fence and compensate its owners rather than leave productive farmland inaccessible and eventually abandoned.

Deputy Chief Minister Prestone Tynsong said the issue had emerged along stretches from Garo Hills to East Jaintia Hills, where landowners and village authorities were not opposed to border fencing but had reservations about what would happen to their land…
"The border fencing is right from Garo Hills up to East Jaintia Hills; the landowners or the village authorities are not against border fencing.
The only issue that the landowners have a reservation about is that once the fencing is completed, the land beyond the fencing will automatically become no man's land.

items.title: 'Green Crackers Rarely Meet Threshold': Experts On Firework Curbs In Delhi
points: Every winter, a familiar trope, a suffocating routine, awaits Delhi.

Research conducted by Dr Manoj Kumar of the Centre for Research on Energy and Clean Air (CREA) revealed that Diwali 2026 was the fourth most polluted day of the year, registering a staggering daily average PM2.5 concentration of 257.
The preceding days - November 5, 6, and 7 - also ranked among the worst air quality days of 2026, securing the sixth, seventh, and eighth spots, respectively.
Diwali 2026 also marked the fourth most polluted Diwali since 2016.

The key debate this year was regarding the manufacturing and marketing of green crackers, developed under the CSIR-NEERI framework to target a minimum 30 per cent reduction in particulate matter compared to conventional variants.

"The CSIR-NEERI framework requires green crackers to demonstrate a minimum 30% reduction in particulate matter emissions compared with conventional crackers or meet prescribed combinations of particulate and gaseous emission reductions.

items.title: Baltic Dry Index climbs to 2862 up 8 points
points: Today, Tuesday, November 10 2026, the Baltic Dry Index climbed 8 points, 2862 points.
Baltic Dry Index is compiled by the London-based Baltic Exchange and covers prices for transported cargo such as coal, grain and iron ore.
The index is based on a daily survey of agents all over the world.

items.title: Recent Ukrainian Attacks Have Reduced Russia’s Oil Processing Capacity By 30%, Sources Say
points: FILE PHOTO: Plumes of smoke rise from fires (centre) at an oil refinery following what the authorities say is a Ukrainian drone strike in the course of the Russia-Ukraine conflict, in Moscow, Russia, September, 20, 2026.

REUTERS/Stringer/File Photo Nov 10 (Reuters) – Renewed Ukrainian drone attacks on Russian oil refineries since late October have reduced Russia’s oil refining capacity by about 30%, two industry sources said.

Ukraine’s attacks on Russian oil refineries add to Moscow’s difficulties in addressing domestic fuel shortages as it ships diesel to international markets under an export deal with US President Donald Trump.
Ukraine has stepped up strikes on Russian refineries since the end of October, when a ceasefire on attacks on energy facilities that Trump announced between Kyiv and Moscow failed to take hold.
Ukrainian attacks disrupted operations and caused emergency situations at nine of Russia’s 35 major refineries over the past week, according to industry sources and officials.

items.title: Qatar LNG Loadings Pick Up to Around Half of Pre-War Levels
points: Photo: RasGas Nov 10, 2026 (Bloomberg) –Liquefied natural gas loadings onto tankers from Qatar have picked up over the past few weeks, suggesting the major exporter is seeking to get more cargoes to the global market despite ongoing disruptions in the…
The number of LNG shipments departing Qatar’s Ras Laffan facility has ranged from 13 to 15 on a 10-day moving average basis so far this month, according to data from Bloomberg, Kpler and Copernicus.
That’s up slightly from an average of about 11 in October, but still roughly half the pre-war pace.
Still, the rise in loadings has yet to translate into a similar bounce in estimated eastbound traffic through the Strait of Hormuz — the waterway that links Qatar with Asia and Europe.
